title: Three Sussex Restaurants Named Among Britain's Best for Indian Food
excerpt: Brighton's Chilli Pickle and Indian Summer and Worthing's BAUJI all made the British Indian Good Food Guide's 2026 list, with The Chilli Pickle also named South Coast Regional Champion.
body:
• Three Sussex restaurants — The Chilli Pickle and Indian Summer in Brighton, and BAUJI in Worthing — have been named in the British Indian Good Food Guide's 2026 list of the country's best Indian food.
  • The Chilli Pickle was also named the guide's South Coast Regional Champion; Indian Summer, on East Street in Brighton, made the Top 100.
  • BAUJI, opened in March 2026 by chef Dayashankar Sharma, is one of 27 new entries this year and was added to the Michelin Guide in August.
  • The national champion was Raval Indian Brasserie & Bar in Newcastle-Gateshead, which took the top title for the second year in a row.

Three Sussex restaurants have secured places in the British Indian Good Food Guide's 2026 national ranking of the country's best Indian food: The Chilli Pickle and Indian Summer, both in Brighton, and BAUJI in Worthing. The guide is an independent publication that selects restaurants on cooking, flavour, consistency, hospitality and the overall dining experience.

The Brighton pair

The Chilli Pickle took the strongest Sussex result, named the guide's South Coast Regional Champion as well as a place on the national list. Indian Summer, on East Street in Brighton, also made the Top 100. The two restaurants anchor a Brighton Indian dining scene that has long punched above the city's size, drawing on the town's large student and visitor trade as well as local regulars.

BAUJI: the new entry

BAUJI in Worthing is among 27 new entries in this year's guide. Opened in March 2026 by chef Dayashankar Sharma, the founder of the Michelin Guide-listed Heritage Dulwich, it serves contemporary Indian comfort food inspired by Sharma's childhood in Rajasthan. The restaurant was added to the Michelin Guide in August and also featured in The Good Food Guide's 100 Best Local Restaurants, where its kitchen is at 67 Rowlands Road, Worthing.

"Bauji bears comparison to places like Gunpowder, Kricket and Cinnamon Kitchen… I would absolutely kill to have it as my local."

— The Good Food Guide, 100 Best Local Restaurants 2026

The Good Food Guide's reviewers singled out BAUJI's signature shatkora jhinga — large grilled prawns with shatkora citrus — and what they called an excellent chicken biryani, while rating the mainstream dishes above the more contemporary interpretations.

The national picture

The guide's national champion for 2026 was Raval Indian Brasserie & Bar in Newcastle-Gateshead, which took the top title for the second year in a row. For Sussex diners, the practical takeaway is simpler: two of the ranked restaurants sit within Brighton's centre and the third is a short trip along the coast in Worthing — three independently judged options for anyone in the county choosing where to eat Indian food this winter.
